text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (P0) — runtime.multigpu.collective: repeated communicator timeouts + intermittent CUDA OOMs observed in tp4 jobs on prod-gpu-pool-3. Affected routes: /v1/generate (hosted), pattern: sustained hangs ~30s then 500. Paging oncall @alex_chan and ops lead @ops_lead_jordan. Auto-created incident channel #inc-2410056789.

alex_chan: ack. I'm on it. Starting by pulling the most recent agent logs from the node that triggered alerts.

sriram_r: I see a flurry of these in the logs earlier — NCCL ERROR: unhandled timeout, then `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in the same process. Might be a KV cache surge + reduced free memory after a recent runtime build. Past incidents had a similar signature when batching bump combined with quantized kernel change.

maya_ingram: confirmed customer reports from observability — token latency spike at 11:41 UTC, request count steady. Stack traces show `ncclCommDestroy` + `cudaMalloc` failures. Putting logs here:

sriram_r: ```
[2026-03-15T11:40:58Z] runtime: nv_peer_mem disabled
[2026-03-15T11:41:01Z] ERROR nccl: NCCL call failed: Timeout on rank 2 of 4 (ncclResult=7)\n stack: at /serving/runtime/collective.cpp:452
[2026-03-15T11:41:03Z] WARNING cuda: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY during allocation 0x7f8c... size=1.2GB\n```

alex_chan: Running `kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=prod-gpu-pool-3` now. Will try a targeted container restart for the pod showing the OOM first. If communicator is stuck, restart should force a new rendezvous and hopefully allow jobs to recover.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: rollback runtime build `release/2026-03-12` -> `release/2026-03-05` (manual authorisation required).

ops_lead_jordan: Hold on rollback unless we confirm regressions in the build. Short-term mitigation options:
- evict problem node from scheduler (cordon + drain) to stop new jobs landing on it
- force fallback to single-GPU serving variant for the most latency-sensitive customer routes
- bump per-worker mem limit and reject large batch sizes at the routing layer

Which do you want prioritized?

alex_chan: Cordoning node now and draining existing GPUs (kubectl cordon/evict). Also initiating a rolling restart of the runtime agent on other nodes where we see the same log signature.

maya_ingram: Setting routing rule to fallback model variant `gpt-lite-solo` for routes matching `/v1/generate` for 15m. This will reduce capacity but keep latency bounded. Notifying affected customers.

eva_cs: Customer impact summary for the pager: two mid-market customers (acme-analytics, holo-systems) saw degraded responses for ~7-12 minutes. No data exfiltration. CS notified both with ETA to full restore next 30m. Flagging acme-analytics as high impact — they have heavy short tail requests.

sriram_r: Quick diagnostic: when NCCL times out the process sometimes leaves stale /var/run/nccl_comm_* sockets and the kernel (!) retains pinned memory. Restarting container clears the sockets but sometimes the driver retains allocations — we should check `nvidia-smi -q` and GPU persistence.

alex_chan: I restarted pod inference-runner-7 on node gpu-03. Pod came back, logs show new rendezvous started and subsequent requests succeeded. However another pod on gpu-07 hit OOM ~2m later. I'm proceeding with node drain on gpu-07 and setting an autoscale to spin up one extra standby node.

ops_lead_jordan: Good. After we stabilize, let's capture core dumps and set env `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and `NCCL_ALGO=ring` on a canary to gather better traces. Also change routing to disallow batching > 8 for the next 1h.

deploy-bot: Rollout: routing config change applied by maya_ingram. env patch queued to canary group (3 nodes) for `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`.

maya_ingram: Added a guard in the API gateway to reject requests that would cause dynamic batching > 8 tokens per request for the affected pool.

eva_cs: Update: acme-analytics reported recovery after the fallback — they're satisfied with status update. Holo-systems still seeing occasional 502s; monitoring closely.

sriram_r: For post-incident follow-up: capture `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` + the runtime logs for the window. Suspect a kernel driver edge-case combined with a recent cuBLAS kernel change.

alex_chan: Handoff to ops_lead_jordan for follow-up and mitigation plan. I'll remain available for triage if more pages. Current status: degraded -> partial service (fallback active), nodes cordoned: gpu-07; rolling restarts performed; autoscale increased by 1. Last observed 5xxs dropping to near-zero after fallback.

ops_lead_jordan: Taking over. Will coordinate postmortem and long-term fix (possible rollback of quantized kernels or runtime memory accounting hardening). Creating PM ticket and assigning to Eng/Runtime + Eng-ML.

pagerbot: Incident status changed to MONITORING. P0 -> P1 in 35m. Incident channel #inc-2410056789 will remain open until postmortem created.

alex_chan: Thanks everyone. Rough timeline/notes saved in the incident channel. I'll add the logs to the ticket before sign-off.
